cards.quote: Moreover, in the strongly acidic medium, aniline is protonated to form the anilinium ion which is meta directing.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: the nitration reaction can be controlled and the ____ can be obtained as the major product
cards.back: the nitration reaction can be controlled and the p-nitro derivative can be obtained as the major product
cards.quote: the nitration reaction can be controlled and the p-nitro derivative can be obtained as the major product

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: on heating with sulphuric acid at 453-473K produces p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid, commonly known as ____, as the major product.
cards.back: on heating with sulphuric acid at 453-473K produces p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid, commonly known as sulphanilic acid, as the major product.
cards.quote: on heating with sulphuric acid at 453-473K produces p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid, commonly known as sulphanilic acid, as the major product.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: They are named by ____ to the name of the parent hydrocarbon from which they are formed, followed by the name of anion such as chloride, hydrogensulphate, etc.
cards.back: They are named by suffixing diazonium to the name of the parent hydrocarbon from which they are formed, followed by the name of anion such as chloride, hydrogensulphate, etc.
cards.quote: They are named by suffixing diazonium to the name of the parent hydrocarbon from which they are formed, followed by the name of anion such as chloride, hydrogensulphate, etc.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: It is readily soluble in water and is ____ but reacts with water when warmed.
cards.back: It is readily soluble in water and is stable in cold but reacts with water when warmed.
cards.quote: It is readily soluble in water and is stable in cold but reacts with water when warmed.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: It ____ in the dry state.
cards.back: It decomposes easily in the dry state.
cards.quote: It decomposes easily in the dry state.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The nitrogen formed escapes from the reaction mixture ____.
cards.back: The nitrogen formed escapes from the reaction mixture as a gas.
cards.quote: The nitrogen formed escapes from the reaction mixture as a gas.
reasons: review:Trivial filler ('escapes as a gas'); blank has no unique fill.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: This is an example of ____.
cards.back: This is an example of electrophilic substitution reaction.
cards.quote: This is an example of electrophilic substitution reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: ____ cannot be prepared by direct halogenation.
cards.back: Aryl fluorides and iodides cannot be prepared by direct halogenation.
cards.quote: Aryl fluorides and iodides cannot be prepared by direct halogenation.
reasons: review:Front has no context ('____ cannot be prepared by direct halogenation'); 'Aryl fluorides and iodides' cannot be derived (alkyl halides etc. also fit).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Thus, the replacement of diazo group by other groups is helpful in preparing those substituted aromatic compounds which cannot be prepared by ____ in benzene or substituted benzene.
cards.back: Thus, the replacement of diazo group by other groups is helpful in preparing those substituted aromatic compounds which cannot be prepared by direct substitution in benzene or substituted benzene.
cards.quote: Thus, the replacement of diazo group by other groups is helpful in preparing those substituted aromatic compounds which cannot be prepared by direct substitution in benzene or substituted benzene.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Presence of amino group in aromatic ring ____ reactivity of the aromatic amines.
cards.back: Presence of amino group in aromatic ring enhances reactivity of the aromatic amines.
cards.quote: Presence of amino group in aromatic ring enhances reactivity of the aromatic amines.
reasons: review:Blank 'enhances' has synonyms (increases); summary point so should be must but the card needs rewording.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which carbohydrate, C6H12O5, does not fit the general formula Cx(H2O)y?
cards.back: Similarly, rhamnose, C6H12O5 is a carbohydrate but does not fit in this definition.
cards.quote: Similarly, rhamnose, C6H12O5 is a carbohydrate but does not fit in this definition.
reasons: review:Rhamnose exception is a one-off trivia example; the idea is already carried by the acetic acid card.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Equation: hydrolysis of sucrose (acid) to glucose and fructose
reasons: review:Equation text carries an extraction artefact ('H2O H+ →'): in print H+ sits over the arrow, so the back does not show NCERT's equation as printed.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms. How are they named?
cards.back: Glucose is found to exist in two different crystalline forms which are named as α and β.
cards.quote: Glucose is found to exist in two different crystalline forms which are named as α and β.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are the α-form and β-form of glucose called?
cards.back: Such isomers, i.e., α-form and β-form, are called anomers.
cards.quote: Such isomers, i.e., α-form and β-form, are called anomers.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is pyran?
cards.back: Pyran is a cyclic organic compound with one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms in the ring.
cards.quote: Pyran is a cyclic organic compound with one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms in the ring.
reasons: review:Definition of pyran is explanatory side text (term naming); pyranose card carries the exam point.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Fructose is an important ____.
cards.back: Fructose is an important ketohexose.
cards.quote: Fructose is an important ketohexose.
reasons: review:Blank 'Fructose is an important ____' has several defensible answers (sugar, monosaccharide, ketose, ketohexose); front should name the ketone and six carbons or ask 'Fructose is a ketose with six carbons, called a ____'.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is furan?
cards.back: Furan is a five membered cyclic compound with one oxygen and four carbon atoms.
cards.quote: Furan is a five membered cyclic compound with one oxygen and four carbon atoms.
reasons: review:Definition of furan is explanatory side text (term naming); furanose card carries the exam point.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In sucrose, between which carbons is the glycosidic linkage, and why is it non-reducing?
cards.back: These two monosaccharides are held together by a glycosidic linkage between C1 of α-D-glucose and C2 of β-D-fructose. Since the reducing groups of glucose and fructose are involved in glycosidic bond formation, sucrose is a non reducing sugar.
cards.quote: These two monosaccharides are held together by a glycosidic linkage between C1 of α-D-glucose and C2 of β-D-fructose. Since the reducing groups of glucose and fructose are involved in glycosidic bond formation, sucrose is a non reducing sugar.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Of which units is maltose composed, and which carbons are linked?
cards.back: Another disaccharide, maltose is composed of two α-D-glucose units in which C1 of one glucose (I) is linked to C4 of another glucose unit (II).
cards.quote: Another disaccharide, maltose is composed of two α-D-glucose units in which C1 of one glucose (I) is linked to C4 of another glucose unit (II).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Of which monosaccharide units is lactose composed?
cards.back: It is composed of β-D-galactose and β-D-glucose.
cards.quote: It is composed of β-D-galactose and β-D-glucose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the chemical structure of amylose?
cards.back: Chemically amylose is a long unbranched chain with 200-1000 α-D-(+)-glucose units held together by C1– C4 glycosidic linkage.
cards.quote: Chemically amylose is a long unbranched chain with 200-1000 α-D-(+)-glucose units held together by C1– C4 glycosidic linkage.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the structure of amylopectin, and where does the branching occur?
cards.back: It is a branched chain polymer of α-D-glucose units in which chain is formed by C1–C4 glycosidic linkage whereas branching occurs by C1–C6 glycosidic linkage.
cards.quote: It is a branched chain polymer of α-D-glucose units in which chain is formed by C1–C4 glycosidic linkage whereas branching occurs by C1–C6 glycosidic linkage.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the basic structural difference of cellulose: its units and linkage?
cards.back: Cellulose is a straight chain polysaccharide composed only of β-D-glucose units which are joined by glycosidic linkage between C1 of one glucose unit and C4 of the next glucose unit.
cards.quote: Cellulose is a straight chain polysaccharide composed only of β-D-glucose units which are joined by glycosidic linkage between C1 of one glucose unit and C4 of the next glucose unit.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Of which carbohydrate is the cell wall of bacteria and plants made up?
cards.back: cellulose
cards.quote: Cell wall of bacteria and plants is made up of cellulose.
reasons: review:Duplicates the plant cell wall point (cellulose card) and the NCERT line says bacterial cell walls are cellulose, which is factually doubtful; avoid teaching it.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Proteins are polymers of which compounds?
cards.back: All proteins are polymers of α-amino acids.
cards.quote: All proteins are polymers of α-amino acids.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which naturally occurring α-amino acid is not optically active, and why are the others?
cards.back: Except glycine, all other naturally occurring α-amino acids are optically active, since the α-carbon atom is asymmetric.
cards.quote: Except glycine, all other naturally occurring α-amino acids are optically active, since the α-carbon atom is asymmetric.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which two types of secondary structure do proteins exist in?
cards.back: They are found to exist in two different types of structures viz. α-helix and β-pleated sheet structure.
cards.quote: They are found to exist in two different types of structures viz. α-helix and β-pleated sheet structure.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the α-helix structure of proteins?
cards.back: α-Helix is one of the most common ways in which a polypeptide chain forms all possible hydrogen bonds by twisting into a right handed screw (helix)
cards.quote: α-Helix is one of the most common ways in which a polypeptide chain forms all possible hydrogen bonds by twisting into a right handed screw (helix)

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the β-pleated sheet structure of proteins?
cards.back: In β-pleated sheet structure all peptide chains are stretched out to nearly maximum extension and then laid side by side which are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
cards.quote: In β-pleated sheet structure all peptide chains are stretched out to nearly maximum extension and then laid side by side which are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are enzymes?
cards.back: This occurs with the help of certain biocatalysts called enzymes. Almost all the enzymes are globular proteins.
cards.quote: This occurs with the help of certain biocatalysts called enzymes. Almost all the enzymes are globular proteins.
reasons: review:Back opens with a dangling 'This occurs with the help of...' (refers to digestion sentence before it) and is not a self-contained defining sentence; use summary line 'Enzymes are biocatalysts which speed up the reactions in biosystems.' (p301).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: James Dewey Watson shared the 1962 Nobel prize in Physiology and Medicine with whom, for the structure of DNA?
cards.back: He is best known for his discovery of the structure of DNA for which he shared with Francis Crick and Maurice Wilkins the 1962 Nobel prize in Physiology and Medicine.
cards.quote: He is best known for his discovery of the structure of DNA for which he shared with Francis Crick and Maurice Wilkins the 1962 Nobel prize in Physiology and Medicine.
reasons: review:Biographical box (Watson Nobel co-winners) is GK filler, not a CUET Chemistry point.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which sugar is present in DNA and which in RNA?
cards.back: In DNA molecules, the sugar moiety is β-D-2-deoxyribose whereas in RNA molecule, it is β-D-ribose.
cards.quote: In DNA molecules, the sugar moiety is β-D-2-deoxyribose whereas in RNA molecule, it is β-D-ribose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Har Gobind Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize for Medicine and Physiology with whom, and for what?
cards.back: Dr Khorana shared the Nobel Prize for Medicine and Physiology in 1968 with Marshall Nirenberg and Robert Holley for cracking the genetic code.
cards.quote: Dr Khorana shared the Nobel Prize for Medicine and Physiology in 1968 with Marshall Nirenberg and Robert Holley for cracking the genetic code.
reasons: review:Biographical box (Khorana Nobel co-winners) is GK filler, not a CUET Chemistry point.
